video_title: Clippers vs. Hornets | Postgame Interviews | Nov. 15, 2026 | LA Clippers

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on the bench unit's consistent energy and impact
quotes.excerpt: they complement our starters very well. When our starters don't have it, we can bring our guys
quotes.quote: They have been good for us all year, all season long. The way they play, they play hard, run the floor, and bring a lot of energy to the game. They complement our starters very well. When our starters don't have it, we can bring our guys off the bench and they have a lot of energy, play the right way, and enjoy playing together.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue praises the Clippers bench unit for their consistent energy and ability to complement the starters throughout the season.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue discusses the impact and energy provided by the bench unit throughout the season.

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on Kobe Brown's late-game turnovers and pressure
quotes.excerpt: It was more we were just trying to slow the game down and just wait for one shot
quotes.quote: It wasn't fair to him. It was more we were just trying to slow the game down and just wait for one shot. They got into him and pressure him and turn the ball over, but usually we are in our flow, so they can't get to his body like that. He was just trying to run the clock down to take one shot, so they pressured him a couple times, so that was on me.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue takes the blame for the late game turnovers involving Kobe Brown, noting he put the young player in a tough spot by trying to run the clock down.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue takes responsibility for late-game turnovers committed by Kobe Brown while trying to run down the clock.

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on the team's halftime adjustment to hit bodies
quotes.excerpt: we know we are small, but we have to hit bodies and pursue the basketball
quotes.quote: Yes, at halftime we were intentional about just talking about, listen, we know we are small, but we have to hit bodies and pursue the basketball. We can't let guys just run free to get the ball because most times they are going to outjump us and they are bigger than we are. We have to make a conscious effort just to make sure that we are hitting bodies and pursuing the basketball.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue on the halftime adjustment to address rebounding issues: We know we are small, but we have to hit bodies and pursue the basketball.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue explains the halftime adjustment to prioritize physical play and rebounding against a larger opponent.

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on Brook's defensive role against Moussa Diabate
quotes.excerpt: you just hit Moussa and just try to keep Moussa off the glass
quotes.quote: Just hitting bodies, trying to be physical. And Brook's job was, you just hit Moussa and just try to keep Moussa off the glass and everybody else has to come back and help rebound. I thought we did a better job in the second half with that. Sometimes you try to hit and pursue the ball. Brook had no responsibilities, just you hit Moussa and then everybody else help come and clean up for you.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue explains the defensive game plan for Brook, tasking him with being physical and keeping Moussa Diabate off the glass.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue details the defensive assignment given to Brook to limit Moussa Diabate on the glass.

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on Max Christie's playmaking ability
quotes.excerpt: his ability to come off screens and defenses are up and they are aware where he is
quotes.quote: It changes a lot, another playmaker. His ability to come off screens and defenses are up and they are aware where he is on the floor. And so for him to be able to turn the corner and make plays like that is huge for our team.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue highlights the impact of Max Christie, noting that his ability to turn the corner and make plays as a secondary playmaker is huge for the team.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue discusses the offensive impact of Max Christie's playmaking ability.

quotes.speaker: Tyronn Lue
quotes.summary_phrase: Tyronn Lue on the team's need to improve rebounding and turnovers
quotes.excerpt: consistently taking care of the basketball. We can't turn the ball over, we understand that
quotes.quote: Consistently taking care of the basketball. We can't turn the ball over, we understand that. And then also rebounding. We are small so we have to hit bodies, we have to pursue the basketball. So those two areas of just rebounding the basketball and taking care of the ball.
quotes.social_post: Tyronn Lue emphasizes the two main areas for improvement: consistently taking care of the basketball and hitting bodies to secure rebounds.

structured.context: Tyronn Lue identifies rebounding and ball security as the primary areas for team improvement.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Ty said that at halftime he was talking to you guys because you guys gave up 15 offensive rebounds in that first half. Just kind of figuring things out in the third quarter. Obviously they went up by 13 in the third, but then obviously you guys made the run. Just what what onus did you guys take it on yourselves as players to make sure that you guys did hit bodies the way that you guys needed to?

text_blocks.speaker: Kobe Brown
text_blocks.text: We knew if we wanted to win the game we had to get our finish our stops with rebounds. That's something we didn't do in the first half and obviously it was something that coach had talked about at halftime was, you know, we got to get these rebounds if we want to win the game. And ultimately that's what it came down to, especially fourth quarter, we really fought hard and and came up with some rebounds that we didn't in the first half and that's what ultimately got us to lead in the win.

quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown credits the team's second half comeback to a renewed focus on hitting bodies and securing defensive rebounds.

structured.context: Kobe Brown reflects on the team's commitment to rebounding in the second half following Tyronn Lue's halftime message.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Brown on the team's unselfishness during their comeback
quotes.excerpt: the unselfishness that we played with. We got the ball moving, we got out on transition
quotes.quote: I think it was just the unselfishness that we played with. We got the ball moving, we got out on transition, got some easy buckets and we knocked down shots. And like I said earlier, we were getting stops and finishing them with rebounds and you know that kind of got us going and being able to get down and play fast and knock down open shots got us the lead.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown says the key to the Clippers comeback was unselfish play and moving the ball to get easy transition buckets.

structured.context: Kobe Brown attributes the team's comeback to unselfish play and defensive stops.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Brown on learning from comeback wins
quotes.excerpt: just knowing what to do and what not to do. When we went down, we obviously weren't
quotes.quote: I think you can learn a lot, just knowing what to do and what not to do. When we went down, we obviously weren't getting stops and then offensively I think we just weren't playing the right way, but then you know when we started getting the stops and playing fast and being unselfish, finding the open man and not worrying about who's taking the shots, everything went well.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown reflects on the comeback win, noting that playing the right way and finding the open man was the difference maker.

structured.context: Kobe Brown discusses the lessons learned from the team's comeback victory.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Brown on adjusting to NBA physicality
quotes.excerpt: I've kind of learned different ways to use it against the defense, especially with foul drawing
quotes.quote: I think I've kind of learned different ways to use it against the defense, especially with foul drawing is a big piece of it. But honestly just when I have the ball in my hands trying to not let them get up into my body and letting them sit there because that's when they can use their physicality against me. So trying to get separation and play a little bit faster going into ball screens and what not just figuring out different ways.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown on adjusting to NBA physicality: I am trying to get separation and play faster going into ball screens to avoid letting defenders get into my body.

structured.context: Kobe Brown explains his adjustments to handling physical defensive pressure in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Brown on his excitement for Giannis Antetokounmpo's return
quotes.excerpt: Man when you come back and he'll be like, man soon he's like it's going to be lob city
quotes.quote: I'm super excited. We've kind of talked a little bit. I'll see him every once in a while and I'll be like, man when you come back and he'll be like, man soon he's like it's going to be lob city. So hopefully we'll get to that and get our chemistry down, but yeah I know he's been working really hard to get back so I'm excited to see him back on the floor.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown is hyped for the return of Giannis Antetokounmpo, saying the two have already talked about bringing Lob City back to the floor.

structured.context: Kobe Brown expresses excitement regarding the impending return of Giannis Antetokounmpo.

quotes.speaker: Kobe Brown
quotes.summary_phrase: Kobe Brown on defensive progression and physicality
quotes.excerpt: you got to be kind of the first one to hit them. You can't let them get downhill
quotes.quote: Definitely, you got to be kind of the first one to hit them. You can't let them get downhill and then bump you first because then it's going to be easy shot for them or they're going to get a foul. So just trying to, you know, be the first to hit them and have the contact higher up in the floor except and not in the paint. And then like you said, like in the post just being strong.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Brown on defensive growth: You have to be the first one to hit them and have the contact higher up the floor instead of in the paint.

structured.context: Kobe Brown describes the importance of initiating physical contact early on defense.
